::: {#sol-linear-input-grad}

Input $h_k$ affects every output $z_j$, so the chain rule adds up a term for each:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\derivf{L}{h_k}
&= \sum_j \derivf{L}{z_j} \derivf{z_j}{h_k}
&& \text{(chain rule through every $z_j$)} \\
&= \sum_j g_j W_{jk}
&& \text{($\partial z_j / \partial h_k = W_{jk}$)} \\
&= \paren{\tp{\matr{W}} \vecf{g}}_k
&& \text{(entry $k$ of a matrix-vector product)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So $\gradwrt{\vhidval} L = \tp{\matr{W}} \vecf{g}$:
the gradient travels back through the layer by the transpose of its weight matrix.

:::
